title: Pressure can feed a cycle
explanation: The example shows how pressure, limited rest and slower progress can reinforce each other. Practical planning, rest or asking for help may address different parts of that pattern.
reflection: Optional reflectionWhere could practical assistance change this fictional cycle?

title: Influence and limits of control
explanation: A reachable action can be worthwhile even when the final outcome depends on other people or wider conditions. Recognizing those limits can help identify where outside assistance is needed.
reflection: Optional reflectionHow can an achievable action coexist with a problem that needs wider support?

title: Grounding with choice
explanation: The activity offers several ways to bring attention toward the current setting. Choice includes keeping eyes open, avoiding body-focused attention, stopping, or selecting another approach.
reflection: Optional reflectionWhat choices keep this exercise voluntary?

title: Notice a thought before following it
explanation: A noticing phrase creates room to consider the action a thought is encouraging. The next step may be practical help or protection when the concern points to a genuine risk.
reflection: Optional reflectionHow does noticing a thought differ from denying a real concern?

title: A routine can stay flexible
explanation: The examples are anchors to adapt, not a timetable to complete. A small change that fits a person’s resources may be more realistic than trying to follow every suggested activity.
reflection: Optional reflectionWhy might a smaller adjustment be more useful than an ideal routine?

title: Organize a pressure and a possible response
explanation: Putting a pressure beside a possible response can help organize what needs attention. The activity can stay entirely unwritten, and a possible response may involve another person or service.
reflection: Optional reflectionHow could this exercise be used without writing anything down?

title: Scenario A: examination pressure
explanation: Pressure and exhaustion can affect attention. The teacher offers practical planning alongside rest; persistent or severe difficulty needs more than a revision schedule.
reflection: Optional reflectionWhat practical help is offered alongside emotional support in this example?

title: Scenario B: financial uncertainty
explanation: Income uncertainty is a material problem as well as an emotional burden. The second scene adds companionship and practical planning without claiming that either removes financial insecurity.
reflection: Optional reflectionWhy would relaxation alone leave an important part of this situation unaddressed?

title: Scenario C: caregiver overload
explanation: Sharing tasks can reduce part of the care burden. Sustainable support may also involve scheduled relief, transport and healthcare conversations.
reflection: Optional reflectionWhich support changes the workload rather than only asking the caregiver to cope?

title: Scenario D: conflict at work
explanation: The worker is seeking private advice rather than being taught to endure mistreatment. Workplace support and safety depend on the actual circumstances.
reflection: Optional reflectionWhy is the safety and fairness of the workplace part of the response?
